How it works

You add a small script to your site. We count your visitors with it and rank projects by that count every week.

What we count

  • Visitors. People our script saw on your site in a day (UTC). Someone who comes back tomorrow counts again tomorrow. A week is the seven days added up, Monday to Sunday.
  • Where they came from. Google, X, Reddit, Hacker News, AI chats like ChatGPT, Product Hunt, our own pages, newsletters, ads, other sites, or direct. Click a source on a project page to see the sites behind it. We keep the site's name only, never the page someone was on.
  • No cookies. Visitors are counted with an anonymous ID that changes every day. We don't store IP addresses, and known bots are filtered out.

The ranking

  • Ordered by visitors. Your project joins the board on the first day we measure it. If we measured fewer than seven days, the table says so.
  • Growth. Week-over-week change, shown once a project has a full previous week with at least 200 visitors, so a jump from 3 to 30 doesn't top the list.
  • Sealed every Monday. The live week keeps changing. On Monday at 00:00 UTC it closes, we review it, and it is published. After that the numbers never change.

Proving it's your site

  • The script is the proof. Every morning we load your homepage and a few pages from your sitemap and look for it.
  • Can't edit the HTML? Add a DNS TXT record instead. You still need the script for anything to be counted.
  • If the script is missing or your site is down, that day isn't measured. It never counts as zero. After seven days without the script, the project is paused until you put it back.
  • We approve every listing by hand. It's free, and approved projects get a followed link from their page.

The badge

  • The link in your snippet turns into a badge with this week's visitor count, the same number as on your page.
  • Three sizes, light or dark. See the badge →

What we don't see

  • Pages without the script, people who block scripts, and anything from before you installed it.
  • Which post or search brought someone. Only the site they came from.
  • Sign-ups, revenue or retention. A number here means people visited, nothing more.
